doc: What the two free judges review: every new or edited lesson line, the rule facts no downloaded rulebook covers, and the research claims SKILL-CURRICULA.md leans on. Code checks come first (VERIFICATION.md); judges are advisory: free models scored 0.575 balanced accuracy on claim checking (MODEL-LINEUP.md), so a 'correct' from both is support, not proof, and any 'wrong' is read by a person.

items.context: Lesson 'One-Hand Form Shots From One Metre'. Evidence: Tran and Silverberg 2008 recommend aiming toward the back of the ring.
items.text: Make one-hand shots from one metre, dropping them past the front rim into the middle of the ring, as each session's first five minutes.

items.context: Lesson 'External Focus Cues: Aim at the Target' (external focus of attention, Wulf).
items.text: Use a cue outside your body, such as drop it past the middle, instead of thinking about your elbow, and compare makes over fifty shots.

items.context: FIBA Official Basketball Rules 2026 v1.0 article 2.5.7; NBA Rule 1 restricted area.
items.text: Compare FIBA's 1.30-metre no-charge semicircle with the NBA's 4-foot arc, balls passing over the backboard, and NBA defensive three seconds as of 2026.

items.context: Inserted after 'Box Score and Shooting Percentages From Your Games'.
items.text: [Analytics] Log Fifty Shots Before Judging a Change | Log fifty attempts over several days before deciding a change worked, because 7 of 10 and 5 of 10 can come from one shooter.

items.context: Inserted after 'Short Daily Sessions Beat One Long Cram'. Contextual-interference research: blocked practice inflates practice performance relative to retention.
items.text: [Practice] Judge Shooting by the Next-Day Cold Set | Take ten elbow jump shots the next day before shooting from the elbow again, because a block of the same shot inflates today's percentage.

items.kind: new lesson line (piano, about ABRSM Grade 2)
items.context: Inserted after 'Shape One Practice Session From Warm-Up to Review'. Abushanab and Bishara 2013: random-order practice retained better at 2 days; learners judged the reverse.
items.text: [Practice] Shuffle Short Units Once Each Plays Correctly | Shuffle your G, D, F and A major scales once each plays correctly, because mixed practice feels harder but your next-day cold take improves.

items.kind: rule fact (as taught in a live lesson)
items.text: In NCAA basketball a team has ten seconds to advance the ball past half court (FIBA and NBA: eight seconds).

items.kind: rule fact (as taught in a live lesson)
items.context: Basketball lesson B05:63, stated as of 2026.
items.text: NFHS (US high school) rules use eight-minute quarters and a three-point arc of 19 ft 9 in, and use a shot clock only in states that adopt one.

items.kind: rule fact (as taught in a live lesson)
items.text: The NBA transition take foul is penalised with one free throw plus possession, except in the last two minutes of the fourth period and overtime, when other rules apply.
In FIBA and NBA basketball the top of the ring is 3.05 m (10 ft) above the floor.

Rosch, Schultz and Honer (2021, IJERPH 18(5):2331) validated a video-based 4-versus-4 passing-decision test for youth basketball: split-half reliability r = 0.92 for accuracy, German U16 national-team players 84% correct versus 57% for a school sports class.

Tran and Silverberg (2008, Journal of Sports Sciences 26(11)) simulated free throws and recommended a launch angle of about 52 degrees, up to about 3 Hz of backspin, and aiming toward the back of the ring.

A 2021 Psychological Bulletin meta-analysis (Chua, Jimenez-Diaz, Lewthwaite, Kim and Wulf) found an external focus of attention beat an internal focus for motor learning, with retention and transfer effects around g = 0.58.

Guadagnoli and Lee (2004, Journal of Motor Behavior 36(2)) proposed the challenge point framework: the practice difficulty that best supports learning depends on the learner's skill level and the task's difficulty.
Kalyuga and Sweller (2005, Educational Technology Research and Development 53) described rapid dynamic assessment of learner expertise (first-step diagnosis) to tailor adaptive e-learning.

Abushanab and Bishara (2013, Memory and Cognition) found that piano-trained participants retained melodies better two days later after random-order practice than after blocked practice, although their own judgments of learning predicted the opposite.
Burgoyne et al. (2019) found that, after serious study and formal instruction were accounted for, tournament play added very little to the explained variance in chess players' peak ratings.

de Bruin, Rikers and Schmidt (2007) found that chess novices learning the king-and-rook-versus-king ending who predicted moves and explained them learned more than those who only predicted or only observed.

The Amsterdam Chess Test (van der Maas and Wagenmakers 2005, American Journal of Psychology) measures chess skill with choose-a-move, predict-a-move, recall and verbal-knowledge tasks and predicts Elo ratings well; adding response times improves validity for easy items.
With the stronger side to move, every legal king-and-queen-versus-king position is a win, and the longest forced mate takes 10 moves; for king-and-rook-versus-king the longest takes 16 moves.

In king and pawn versus king with a pawn not on the a- or h-file, if the attacking king stands on one of the pawn's key squares (for a pawn on the 2nd to 4th rank: the three squares two ranks in front of it) and the pawn cannot be captured at once, the attacker wins whoever is to move.

The NBA and USA Basketball Youth Guidelines set maximum organised basketball of 3 hours a week for ages 7-8, 5 for ages 9-11, 10 for ages 12-14 and 14 for high school, with at least 2, 2, 1 and 1 rest days a week.
